official.deadline_note: Institutional deadlines differ per faculty and graduate school: Amsterdam Law School LLM and Faculty of Science MSc AMS: 15 January at 23:59 CET; Graduate School of Social Sciences: 15 February 2027, 23:59 CET (final date, no late applications); UvA Economics and Business Master's: 15 January for the September intake; Economics and Business Bachelor's: 15 January for Business Administration and Economics and Business Economics, 1 March for all other E&B Bachelor's programmes.
official.application_cycle: 2027/2028 cycle (September 2027 start); Humanities LLAMS figures still shown for academic year 2026-2027 while the page is updated for 2027-2028
official.status_note: The Faculty of Science has published its September 2027 round: one Amsterdam Merit Scholarship of EUR 26,125, selection in March and decisions in April. The Amsterdam Law School lists its 2027-2028 AMS with the amount 'to be announced', and the Graduate School of Social Sciences has published a final 15 February 2027 deadline. The UvA states scholarship amounts are determined each year and published on the website in the late autumn, and that no rights can be derived from information about previous years.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording (Graduate School of Social Sciences): 'The scholarship equals the tuition fee. Please note that the scholarship cannot be used as a (partial) tuition waiver. The applicant must still pay the full amount of tuition due, and can do this in instalments. Scholarship holders will also receive their grant in monthly instalments.' The Faculty of Science page adds: 'The scholarship cannot be used as a (partial) tuition fee waiver; the AMS recipient must still pay the full amount of tuition fee (with the possibility to pay this amount in monthly instalments).'
official.funding_period: one-off; equal to the programme's tuition fee
benefits: Amsterdam Merit Scholarship with a value equal to the tuition fee; Faculty of Science: 'For the September 2027 start only one Amsterdam Merit Scholarship (AMS) of EUR 26,125 will be awarded', paid in monthly instalments

UvA Economics and Business Master's AMS: 'The value of the scholarship is equal to the tuition fee + EUR 5,000 additional allowance for the duration of the programme (1 year, without prolongation)', paid in 12 equal instalments

Letje Lips Amsterdam Merit Scholarship, Graduate School of Humanities: 'For the academic year 2026-2027, four (4) LLAMS scholarships of EUR 37,500 are available' for students from a non-privileged background

Bachelor's AMS: a few scholarships each year (Economics and Business awarded 1 scholarship per programme last year; Psychology nominates 1 student per September intake); UvA Bachelor's programme pages publish a value of EUR 6,000 per year (total EUR 18,000) from the previous cycle

Scholarship continuation for subsequent year(s) depends on satisfactory study progress (approx. 80% of credits in any one year; Faculty of Science requires at least 40 ECTS in year one of a two-year programme)
eligibility: Hold a non-EU/EEA passport (Faculty of Science: no EU/EEA or Suisse nationality; Economics and Business: non-EU nationality only)
Not be eligible for support under the Dutch system of study grants and loans (Studiefinanciering) and/or the low tuition fee rate
Not receive a full coverage scholarship for the same period of study as the AMS

Submit a complete application to a UvA degree programme before the scholarship deadline; be admitted for the first time to a UvA Master's (Faculty of Science: previous academic programme completed no longer than 3 years ago)
Be able to comply with Dutch visa regulations (IND) and enrol as a full-time student for the academic year

Faculty-specific academic bars: Faculty of Science top 10% of graduates (GPA 3.5 USA 4-point scale / 1st class honours UK / 8+ Dutch 10-point scale); Amsterdam Law School GPA comparable to 4.0 (USA), first class honours (UK) or 8.0 (Dutch 10-point) restricted to four LLM programmes; UvA Economics and Business at least (Magna) Cum Laude, first-class honours or 3.7 (USA)
requirements: Motivation letter: maximum 500 words (Faculty of Science and Amsterdam Law School) or maximum 300 words (UvA Economics and Business, including Bachelor's)

Graduate School of Social Sciences: one self-composed PDF file containing curriculum vitae, scholarship motivation letter, letter of recommendation and financial plan, uploaded in SIS under 'Additional documents' as the 'scholarship motivation letter'

UvA Economics and Business: recommendation letter by a dean, teacher or academic supervisor that also confirms you belong to the top 10% of your class or year, plus proof of English proficiency and, if applicable, GMAT/GRE
Complete degree programme application via Studielink and SIS, with the scholarship consideration box ticked, before the deadline

Bachelor's Economics and Business: single PDF scholarship motivation letter (max 300 words) including name, UvAnetID, programme, previous education, GPA, matching/selection participation, English test score and a recommendation letter
Humanities LLAMS: certified documents (diploma or graduation statement, final transcripts) by the faculty's August deadline and ability to pay housing and immigration fees before arrival
documents: Curriculum vitae (part of the Graduate School of Social Sciences AMS package)

Scholarship motivation letter (300 words at UvA Economics and Business; 500 words at Faculty of Science and Amsterdam Law School; Graduate School of Social Sciences asks how the programme fulfils personal and academic goals)

Letter of recommendation written by a professor or another member of academic staff (Graduate School of Social Sciences); recommendation letter by a dean, teacher or academic supervisor confirming top 10% class standing (Economics and Business); recommendation letter by a dean, teacher or academic supervisor (Bachelor's Economics and Business)
Financial plan showing that you need the scholarship and have sufficient funds to cover all other costs (Graduate School of Social Sciences)

Proof of English proficiency: TOEFL iBT overall 100 (minimum 22 per component), IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (7.0 per component; 6.5 possible), Cambridge CAE or CPE 190 per skill, LanguageCert Academic 70 (minimum 65 per subscore), PTE Academic 71 (minimum 65 per subscore), taken no more than two years before enrolment (UvA Economics and Business; exemptions for secondary diplomas from Australia, Canada except Quebec, Ireland, New Zealand, South Africa, the UK or the US)
GMAT/GRE test score if applicable to the programme, with at least the expected scores (UvA Economics and Business)
Complete UvA degree programme application in Studielink and SIS (the scholarship application is rendered invalid without it)
selection_criteria: Academic excellence and promise in the proposed field, as evidenced by academic records (Graduate School of Social Sciences, Faculty of Science)
Quality of the letter of motivation (Graduate School of Social Sciences, Faculty of Science)

Quality of the candidate's curriculum vitae including extracurricular activities such as student commissions, international experience, high-level sports or music, or volunteer work (Faculty of Science)
Amsterdam Law School: 'The AMS scholarship will be awarded through a lottery system' - random selection from applicants who meet the requirements

Bachelor's Economics and Business: excellent GPA (for example 90-100% / A-A+) plus an excellent UvA Matching or selection test result; Psychology nominates candidates whose selection test score is in the best 10%

Selection takes place in March (Faculty of Science, Graduate School of Social Sciences); UvA Economics and Business awarded 12 scholarships from 150 applications last year; the Graduate School of Social Sciences awarded 2 scholarships in 2025 (1.5% of applications)
coverage: Published wording: 'The scholarship equals the tuition fee. Please note that the scholarship cannot be used as a (partial) tuition waiver. The applicant must still pay the full amount of tuition due, and can do this in instalments. Scholarship holders will also receive their grant in monthly instalments.'
Graduate School of Humanities states the LLAMS 'does not cover the full amount of your study and stay at the University of Amsterdam'
UvA Economics and Business Master's AMS adds a EUR 5,000 additional allowance on top of the tuition fee, paid in 12 equal monthly instalments on a reimbursement basis
No living-cost, travel or installation coverage is published for any current scheme; Faculty of Science requires applicants to 'have sufficient funds to cover all other costs'
application_method: Master's AMS in general: apply first to the degree programme and tick the box in the application form asking whether you want to be considered for a UvA scholarship; the AMS application is part of the Master's programme application procedure

Graduate School of Social Sciences: submit the study programme application in SIS, then upload the single self-composed PDF (CV, scholarship motivation letter, letter of recommendation, financial plan) under 'Additional documents' as 'scholarship motivation letter'; an AMS application without a timely programme application is invalid

UvA Economics and Business (Master's): apply via Studielink and the online application form (SIS) and upload the recommendation letter and 300-word motivation letter under the scholarship section; OnCampus, E&B and rMSc students apply via the faculty form

Amsterdam Law School: on the 'Scholarship' tab of the LLM application select the AMS (and optionally the Mr Julia Henriette Jaarsma-Adolfs Fund Scholarship), then upload the scholarship motivation letter on the 'Additional documents' tab; missing either step makes the scholarship application incomplete

Bachelor's Economics and Business: apply via Studielink and SIS 'My Applications', tick the scholarship consideration box, register for the early selection/matching rounds and upload the single scholarship motivation letter PDF under 'Additional Documents'

Humanities LLAMS: submit the Master's application in SIS by the deadline, then complete the separate LLAMS application form (opened from early December); the two applications are reviewed by different committees
official.application_route: Online: complete the UvA degree programme application via Studielink and SIS, tick the UvA scholarship consideration box, and upload the faculty-specific scholarship documents before that faculty's deadline.
official.study_mode: full-time (applicants must enrol as full-time students for the academic year)
official.citizenship_residency: Non-EU/EEA nationality required (Faculty of Science also excludes Swiss nationals); applicants must not be eligible for the Dutch study grants and loans system (Studiefinanciering) or the low EEA tuition fee rate
official.international_eligibility: Yes, but only for students from outside the EU/EEA; EU/EEA nationals are excluded from these schemes
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Scheme-specific: Faculty of Science MSc programmes; Amsterdam Law School LLMs in International and European Law, Transnational and European Private Law, Law & Finance, and International Criminal Law only; Graduate School of Social Sciences Master's programmes (pre-Master's candidates excluded, except the summer-school-only exception); Graduate School of Humanities one-year non-selective English-taught Master's (Research and Dual Master's not eligible); UvA Economics and Business Bachelor's and Master's programmes)
official.duration: Master's: one-year programmes (12 monthly instalments at Economics and Business); two-year programmes require at least 40 ECTS in year one for continuation (Faculty of Science)
official.description: The University of Amsterdam states it 'aims to attract the world's brightest students to its international classrooms' and offers the Amsterdam Merit Scholarship to outstanding students from outside the EU/EEA planning a Master's programme, alongside faculty-specific scholarship schemes for international Master's and Bachelor's students. The scholarship equals the tuition fee, is paid in monthly instalments, and cannot be used as a (partial) tuition waiver.
official.program_type: Merit scholarship for international students with a tuition-level value, administered separately by each faculty
official.english_requirement: Published by UvA Economics and Business: TOEFL iBT overall score of 100 (minimum 22 per component), IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 per component; a subscore of 6.5 is accepted), Cambridge CAE or CPE 190 points overall and in each skill, LanguageCert Academic minimum total 70 with 65 per subscore, or PTE Academic minimum total 71 with 65 per subscore, taken no more than two years before enrolment. Exemptions for secondary school diplomas from schools in and accredited by Australia, Canada (except Quebec), Ireland, New Zealand, South Africa, the UK or the US. Individual programmes may set their own admission language requirements.

not_confirmed: 2027-2028 AMS amounts for faculties other than the Faculty of Science (Amsterdam Law School states the amount is 'to be announced'; Humanities LLAMS still publishes academic year 2026-2027 figures while the page is being updated for 2027-2028)

Current-cycle Bachelor's AMS amount: programme tuition-fee pages still show EUR 6,000 per year (EUR 18,000 total) from a previous cycle, while the faculty states amounts are determined annually and published in late autumn; the Psychology page says the amount will be announced later
Living-cost, travel and installation coverage: not published for any current scheme except the faculty-specific EUR 5,000 Economics and Business Master's allowance
A single central application deadline: the UvA states deadlines differ per faculty or graduate school
verification.notes: All facts taken from the UvA's own domains (uva.nl and gsh.uva.nl): the Fees and funding hub, Master's and Bachelor's scholarship hubs, and the Faculty of Science, Amsterdam Law School, Graduate School of Social Sciences, UvA Economics and Business (Master's and Bachelor's) and Graduate School of Humanities pages. The recorded amount is the Faculty of Science's published September 2027 AMS figure of EUR 26,125.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a tuition-level award rather than a full ride: the grant is paid out in monthly instalments and you must still pay the full tuition fee yourself while proving you can fund living costs. Because awards per faculty are extremely scarce (one Science MSc AMS, one Law AMS, four Humanities scholarships), your degree programme application is effectively the scholarship application, and the published GPA bar is the real filter. Deadlines are faculty-specific - most run to 15 January 2027, but the Graduate School of Social Sciences extends to 15 February 2027 and Economics and Business sets a separate 1 March round for some Bachelor's programmes.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent non-EU/EEA graduates with top-decile academic records applying for a full-time UvA Master's (Science, Law, Social Sciences, Humanities or Economics and Business) who can independently fund Amsterdam living costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit the Studielink and SIS programme application first and tick the UvA scholarship consideration box; without a timely programme application the scholarship application is invalid

Build the faculty-specific scholarship PDF early: the Graduate School of Social Sciences requires CV, motivation letter, recommendation letter and financial plan in one self-composed PDF, in that order
Write the motivation letter to the exact word cap (300 words Economics and Business, 500 words Faculty of Science and Law) and address both merit and, for Social Sciences, demonstrated financial need
Book an English test early if you have no exemption; scores must be no more than two years old at enrolment, and GMAT/GRE may be expected for Economics and Business programmes
Prepare proof of funds for living expenses: the UvA indicates roughly EUR 900-1,500 per month in Amsterdam excluding tuition, and visa procedures depend on it
common_rejection_risks: Missing the faculty-specific deadline: assuming the hub's earliest date covers you, when Social Sciences runs to 15 February 2027 and Economics and Business Bachelor's has a separate 1 March round

Uploading scholarship documents in the wrong slot: the PDF must go under 'Additional documents' as the 'scholarship motivation letter', and the Law application also needs the scholarship tab completed
Exceeding the motivation letter word limit, or submitting a recommendation letter that does not explicitly confirm top-10% class or year standing where that is required

Losing eligibility through nationality or funding rules: EU/EEA or Swiss nationals, students entitled to the low EEA fee or Studiefinanciering, and holders of other full-coverage scholarships for the same period are excluded
Applying through a pre-Master's pathway at Humanities or Social Sciences, where pre-Master's students are not awarded the scholarship (only the Social Sciences summer-school-only exception applies)
For two-year awards, dropping below roughly 80% of credits per year or under 40 ECTS in year one, which ends continuation
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything beyond the tuition-level value: Amsterdam living costs the UvA indicates at roughly EUR 900-1,500 per month including rent, plus housing and immigration fees, health insurance and study materials. Humanities explicitly states the LLAMS does not cover the full amount of stay and study, and Economics and Business Bachelor's applicants must cover any tuition above the published award.
document_audit: One-PDF rule at the Graduate School of Social Sciences: CV, motivation letter, recommendation letter and financial plan must be combined in a single self-composed PDF in the required order
Word caps differ by faculty (300 vs 500 words), so verify the faculty page rather than the central hub before drafting
Economics and Business recommendation letters must explicitly confirm top-10% class or year standing, not merely endorse the applicant
Bachelor's Economics and Business allows only one uploaded document, so the 300-word letter must also carry GPA, English score, matching/selection participation and the recommendation
Humanities award holders must hand in certified diploma and final transcripts by the faculty's August date even after selection, and pre-pay housing and immigration fees around May-June
alerts: Deadline map: 15 January (Faculty of Science, Amsterdam Law School, Economics and Business Master's, most Economics and Business Bachelor's programmes), 15 February 2027 (Graduate School of Social Sciences), 1 March (other Economics and Business Bachelor's programmes)

Amounts are set annually and published in late autumn; the UvA warns that no rights can be derived from previous years' figures, so revisit the faculty page in late 2026 for the confirmed 2027-2028 value
The Amsterdam Law School allocates its single AMS by lottery among eligible applicants, so eligibility completeness matters more than ranking
Continuation requires approximately 80% of credits in any one year, and Faculty of Science two-year awards need at least 40 ECTS in the first year
Notify the scholarship office of any change in nationality, residence permit type or additional financial support during the academic year

Competition is extreme: 12 awards from 150 applications at Economics and Business and 2 awards (1.5% of applications) at the Graduate School of Social Sciences recently, so keep an external funding fallback ready
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Programme application in Studielink and SIS before the faculty deadline with the scholarship box ticked, then the faculty-specific scholarship document uploaded in SIS (or the separate Humanities form); faculty committees decide in March-May and pay the grant in monthly instalments.
